title: EchoPilot
oneLine: A tool that lets a small business owner run their Google Business Profile over SMS, so they can answer reviews and change hours without opening a dashboard.

hero.alt: Generated stand-in image for EchoPilot. Not a photograph of the real build.

intake.question: What is it, in one sentence?
intake.draft: A product that lets small business owners manage their Google Business Profile entirely over SMS: respond to reviews, update hours, post updates, request reviews from customers, without ever opening a dashboard.

intake.question: Role, timeline, status
intake.draft: Solo. First commit 6 December 2025, last 20 January 2026, 5 commits. Built: marketing site. Not built: the product. Planned stack was Next.js on Vercel, Fastify on Railway, Supabase, Twilio, Google Business Profile API, Stripe.

intake.question: What made it hard?
intake.hint: Was Google verification really the blocker?
intake.draft: From your own docs, the blocker was not code: a 60 day Google Business Profile verification requirement and the Google API approval process, plus Twilio approval. That is a genuinely interesting constraint and it is the honest story of this project.

intake.question: What did you decide, and what did you reject?
intake.draft: The decision documented across your files is SMS as the primary interface with AI as an optional helper and the dashboard secondary. That is a real and slightly contrarian product call. The rejected alternative is the dashboard-first SaaS everyone else builds.

intake.question: What number can you put on it?
intake.hint: How many businesses did you actually talk to?
intake.draft: 12 planning documents, echopilot.me registered. NEEDS YOU: how far did the Google verification actually get, and did you talk to any Boulder businesses? You have a boulder-business-outreach.md, so presumably yes. How many?

intake.question: What broke, and what did you do?
intake.draft: NEEDS YOU: what stopped it. Google approval, time, or losing interest? Any of those is a fine answer and the third one is the most common.

intake.question: What media do you have?
intake.draft: The marketing site, the brand guide, and the architecture from stack.md.

intake.question: What would you do differently?
intake.hint: Two sentences. Not self criticism, a design judgement you would make differently now.
